hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 adheres more tightly to some recycling receptors than APOE3, impeding recycling.
A: APOE genotype or apoE isoform (APOE4 vs APOE3)
B: binding/adhesion strength of apoE to recycling receptors (ApoER2, LRP1, LDLR, VLDLR...) and the resulting impeded receptor recycling
scope: IN: binding strength or kinetics of apoE isoforms to recycling receptors (ApoER2/LRP8, LRP1, LDLR, VLDLR, heparan sulfate when tied to receptor recycling), pH-dependent dissociation in endosomes, and receptor surface levels/recycling impeded by apoE4 (e.g. ApoER2, glutamate receptors trapped in endosomes), including rescues (NHE6 inhibition) in apoE4 conditions. OUT: receptor-independent effects, binding to non-recycling partners, downstream synaptic function without a receptor-recycling readout.

row.Finding description: Both lipidated ApoE3 and ApoE4 reduced surface LDLR relative to ApoE2 in APOE-knockout human iPSC-derived astrocytes, without an established additional ApoE4 effect.
row.Finding quote: In H4, WT HAP1, and APOE KO iAstrocytes, incubation with lipApoE3/E4 significantly reduced surface LDLR relative to lipApoE2, revealing impaired LDLR recycling accompanying increased LDLR-mediated lipApoE uptake (Figure 2A–D, Figure S2A–B).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (shared astrocyte surface-LDLR depletion; E4-specific additional impairment unresolved)
row.Experimental system: Human iPSC-derived astrocytes differentiated from an APOE-knockout clone of ThermoFisher A18945, originally APOE3/3; exogenous POPC-lipidated ApoE at 10 μg/mL for one day; surface LDLR immunostaining.

proposed.why: Isoform varied but the readout is steady surface level of an apoE-binding receptor, a surrogate B' for impeded recycling (endocytosis or synthesis could also move it), so class 3, strength 2, same as every other surface-level row. (was 1/1)

row.Finding description: One-day pretreatment with either lipidated ApoE3 or ApoE4 nearly abolished subsequent LDL uptake, consistent with impaired surface-LDLR availability but without an established extra ApoE4 effect.
row.Finding quote: When DiI-LDL was spiked into media after 1d pre-treatment with lipApoE3/E4, DiI-LDL uptake was nearly abolished (Figure 2K, L).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (shared near-abolition of subsequent LDL uptake)
row.Experimental system: Human H4 neuroglioma cells; 10 μg/mL POPC-lipidated ApoE for one day, followed by 10 μg/mL DiI-LDL for 3–4 h; live confocal imaging.

proposed.why: Receptor localization in early/recycling compartments (or cellular apoE-receptor association) is a surrogate B' for trapping, scored class 3, strength 3 like every other such colocalization row. (was 3/2)

row.Finding description: Without insulin, nearly 20% of IR-GFP colocalized with transferrin-positive endosomes after apoE4, with less colocalization after apoE3, across three independent experiments.
row.Finding quote: In the absence of insulin, we found that nearly 20% of IR-GFP co-localized with transferrin in the endosomal compartment in apoE4-treated cells whereas less co-localization was observed in apoE3-treated cells (Figures 6A and 6D).
row.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (greater insulin-receptor localization in transferrin-positive endosomes)
row.Experimental system: Human SH-SY5Y cells expressing human IR-GFP; overnight 100 nM recombinant apoE, no insulin; Alexa568-transferrin at 20 μg/ml for one hour; confocal colocalization analysis.

proposed.why: Receptor localization in early/recycling compartments (or cellular apoE-receptor association) is a surrogate B' for trapping, scored class 3, strength 3 like every other such colocalization row. (was 3/2)

row.Finding description: At 60 minutes, apoE4-treated neurons retained significantly more internalized insulin receptor than apoE3-treated neurons, indicating delayed receptor recycling.
row.Finding quote: After 60 minutes treatment with apoE3, the amount of internalized (biotinylated) IR was reduced, reflecting a membrane recycling of IR and subsequent biotin cleavage. Interestingly, apoE4-treated cells exhibited significantly more intracellular IR compared to those treated with apoE3 at 60 minutes, suggesting a delayed recycling of IR in the presence of apoE4 (Figure S8A).
row.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (greater intracellular insulin-receptor retention at 60 minutes)
row.Experimental system: Primary cortical neurons from embryonic Apoe−/− mice; surface proteins labeled with cleavable biotin at 4°C, then 100 nM recombinant apoE at 37°C; surface stripping and intracellular insulin-receptor immunoblotting.

proposed.why: Isoform varied and return of internalized receptor to the surface measured directly (B itself), so class 1, strength 1, matching the other receptor-recycling chase assays. (was 3/2)

row.Experimental system: Hamster CHO-S cells stably expressing murine sortilin in apoE3- or apoE4-conditioned medium; surface receptors antibody-labeled at 4 °C, internalized for 15 minutes at 37 °C, then assessed after 60 minutes with dynasore at 37 °C. Immunostaining of permeabilized versus non-permeabilized cells distinguished total and surface receptor pools.

proposed.why: Isoform varied and return of internalized receptor to the surface measured directly (B itself), so class 1, strength 1, matching the other receptor-recycling chase assays. (was 1/2)

row.Finding description: Across three independent experiments in primary mouse neurons treated with Reelin, human ApoE4 reduced surface ApoER2 more than ApoE3.
row.Finding quote: Receptor surface levels show a stronger reduction with ApoE4 than ApoE3.
row.Finding summary: (ApoE3 -> ApoE4) -> (lower neuronal surface ApoER2 during Reelin stimulation)
row.Experimental system: Primary cortical neurons isolated from E18 Slc9a6 wildtype mouse embryos, with female Slc9a6+/+ and male Slc9a6y/+ littermates represented; no AD-model mutation reported for this assay. At DIV10–14, neurons received human ApoE3 or ApoE4 conditioned medium from transfected HEK293 cells, 5 μg/ml for 30 minutes, followed by Reelin, 2 μg/ml for another 30 minutes. Surface ApoER2 was measured by sulfo-NHS-SS-biotin labeling, NeutrAvidin isolation, and immunoblotting, with total receptor immunoblots. This measures receptor surface availability as a recycling readout, not apoE binding strength or dissociation kinetics; the brain cells were mouse, not human.

proposed.why: Isoform varied but the readout is steady surface level of an apoE-binding receptor, a surrogate B' for impeded recycling (endocytosis or synthesis could also move it), so class 3, strength 2, same as every other surface-level row. (was 1/2)

row.Finding description: Across three independent experiments, germline NHE6 deletion completely restored the ApoER2 recycling readout in primary mouse neurons exposed to human ApoE4 and Reelin.
row.Finding quote: Apoer2 recycling was completely restored in Slc9a6- neurons treated with ApoE4 (Figure 4C).
row.Finding summary: (NHE6 present -> NHE6 deleted, with ApoE4) -> (restored neuronal surface ApoER2)
row.Experimental system: Primary cortical neurons from E18 germline Slc9a6-knockout mouse embryos and wildtype littermates, including female Slc9a6-/- and male Slc9a6y/- knockouts; no AD-model mutation reported. At DIV10–14, cultures received HEK293-secreted human ApoE4 at 5 μg/ml for 30 minutes, followed by Reelin at 2 μg/ml for another 30 minutes. Surface biotinylation and immunoblotting quantified ApoER2 surface availability. Endosomal pH and apoE–receptor binding were not measured in this neuronal panel; the cells were mouse, not human.

proposed.why: A is held at APOE4 and a path variable (NHE6/endosomal pH) is manipulated, which does not perturb A even as a surrogate, so class 5 (rescue tests mediation, not A->B); strength one step below the matching isoform readout. (was 2/3)

row.Finding description: LRP1 knockdown reduced APOER2 early-endosomal colocalization in APOE4 neurons by a reported 38.8%, assessed in 50–53 cells from five preparations.
row.Finding quote: As can be seen, the downregulation of LRP1 had no significant effects on the total levels of the receptors, had no effect on the size of early endosomes (not shown), but did abolish the excess colocalization of these receptors with early endosomes in APOE4 neurons (the percent of reduction when compared to APOE4 control equals to 38.8% in APOER2, 48.9% in IR, and 64.1% in VEGFR).
row.Finding summary: (LRP1 knockdown in APOE4 neurons) -> (lower fraction of APOER2 colocalizing with early endosomes)
row.Experimental system: Brain-derived primary neurons from neonatal human-APOE4 targeted-replacement mice on an α-synuclein-null background; AAV9 LRP1 gRNA plus Cas9 at DIV3; collection ten days later per CRISPR methods; APOER2/Rab5 confocal M1 analysis in transduced cells.
row.Data location: Fig. 12B, APOER2, APOE4-LRP1 AAv versus APOE4 control

proposed.why: A is held at APOE4 and a receptor knockdown or broad drug (path variable) is manipulated with a localization or indirect readout, so class 5, strength 4. (was 4/3)

row.Finding description: APOER2 knockdown in APOE4 neurons caused no significant difference in LRP1 colocalization with early endosomes.
row.Finding quote: Additionally, knock-down of APOER2 did not affect the intracellular localization of LRP1.
row.Finding summary: (APOER2 knockdown in APOE4 neurons) -> (no change in LRP1 colocalization with early endosomes)
row.Experimental system: Brain-derived primary neurons from neonatal human-APOE4 targeted-replacement mice on an α-synuclein-null background; AAV9 APOER2 gRNA plus Cas9 at DIV3; collection ten days later per CRISPR methods; LRP1/Rab5 confocal M1 analysis in transduced cells.
row.Data location: Fig. 13B, LRP1, APOE4-APOER2 AAv versus APOE4 control

proposed.why: A is held at APOE4 and a receptor knockdown or broad drug (path variable) is manipulated with a localization or indirect readout, so class 5, strength 4. (was 4/3)

row.Finding description: APOER2 knockdown reduced VEGFR2 early-endosomal colocalization in APOE4 neurons by 52.6%, assessed in 24–28 cells from three preparations.
row.Finding quote: A different pattern was observed with the growth factor receptors IR and VEGFR, where knocking down APOER2 increased the levels of IR (50.9% increase relative to APOE4 control) and VEGFR (21.3% increase relative to APOE4 control) in APOE4 neurons and decreased their colocalization with early endosomes (IR: 55.1% reduction, and VEGFR: 52.6% reduction relative to APOE4 control).
row.Finding summary: (APOER2 knockdown in APOE4 neurons) -> (lower fraction of VEGFR2 colocalizing with early endosomes)
row.Experimental system: Brain-derived primary neurons from neonatal human-APOE4 targeted-replacement mice on an α-synuclein-null background; AAV9 APOER2 gRNA plus Cas9 at DIV3; collection ten days later per CRISPR methods; VEGFR2/Rab5 confocal M1 analysis in transduced cells.
row.Data location: Fig. 13B, VEGFR2, APOE4-APOER2 AAv versus APOE4 control

proposed.why: A is held at APOE4 and a receptor knockdown or broad drug (path variable) is manipulated with a localization or indirect readout, so class 5, strength 4. (was 4/3)

row.Finding description: LRP1 knockdown reduced VEGFR2 early-endosomal colocalization in APOE4 neurons by 64.1%, assessed in 23–27 cells from three preparations.
row.Finding quote: As can be seen, the downregulation of LRP1 had no significant effects on the total levels of the receptors, had no effect on the size of early endosomes (not shown), but did abolish the excess colocalization of these receptors with early endosomes in APOE4 neurons (the percent of reduction when compared to APOE4 control equals to 38.8% in APOER2, 48.9% in IR, and 64.1% in VEGFR).
row.Finding summary: (LRP1 knockdown in APOE4 neurons) -> (lower fraction of VEGFR2 colocalizing with early endosomes)
row.Experimental system: Brain-derived primary neurons from neonatal human-APOE4 targeted-replacement mice on an α-synuclein-null background; AAV9 LRP1 gRNA plus Cas9 at DIV3; collection ten days later per CRISPR methods; VEGFR2/Rab5 confocal M1 analysis in transduced cells.
row.Data location: Fig. 12B, VEGFR2, APOE4-LRP1 AAv versus APOE4 control

proposed.why: A is held at APOE4 and a receptor knockdown or broad drug (path variable) is manipulated with a localization or indirect readout, so class 5, strength 4. (was 4/3)

row.Finding description: Insulin-receptor late-endosomal colocalization was 25.80% lower in APOE4 than APOE3 neurons, measured in 25–37 cells from two to three preparations.
row.Finding quote: This decrease in late endosomes was significant for both IR and VEGFR with a similar trend observed in APOER2 (IR: 25.80% decrease, p < 0.05; VEGFR: 47.74% decrease, p < 0.05; APOER2 : 22.09% decrease, p = 0.156).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower fraction of insulin receptor colocalizing with late endosomes)
row.Experimental system: Brain-derived neuron-enriched primary cultures from 1–3-day-old human-APOE3/4 targeted-replacement mice on an α-synuclein-null background; DIV21; insulin-receptor/Rab7 double staining, confocal microscopy and M1 colocalization.

proposed.why: Late-endosome/lysosome colocalization is weakly coupled to recycling (degradation is an alternative route), so class 3, strength 4, same for every receptor in this assay. (was 3/3)

row.Finding description: Adding apoE4 changed the reported axotomy response from unchanged surface LRP8 without exogenous human apoE to increased surface LRP8, rather than reduced surface availability.
row.Finding quote: With no exogenous human ApoE particles added, axotomy elevated pTyr416 phospho-Src family levels moderately, but did not alter LRP8 distribution. In the presence of added E2, axotomy reduced surface LRP8 and strongly suppressed Src activation. In stark contrast, cultures with E4 showed increased surface LRP8 and Src activation after axotomy.
row.Finding summary: (no added human apoE -> added apoE4) -> (axotomy-associated increase in surface LRP8)
row.Experimental system: Primary cortical neurons from P1 wild-type mice with endogenous mouse ApoE; day-7 axotomy; purified human apoE4 lipoparticles, 12 µg/ml, added 24 hours later versus no exogenous human apoE; day-12 reelin exposure and surface-biotinylation LRP8 immunoblot.

proposed.why: Comparator is no added apoE, not apoE3, so apoE4 addition is a surrogate A' (any apoE ligand drives receptor internalization, shown in P7) and surface/internalized receptor is a surrogate B': class 4, strength 4. (was 4/3)

row.Finding description: Surface LRP5 immunoblots were reported to show no apoE-isoform regulation across axotomy conditions, including no significant difference reported between apoE4 and apoE3.
row.Finding quote: In contrast to LRP8, surface localization of LRP5 and LRP6 was not regulated by axotomy of ApoE (Fig. S4E–S4H).
row.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (no change in surface LRP5)
row.Experimental system: P1 wild-type mouse primary cortical neurons from the Fig. 4J experiment; purified human apoE3 or apoE4 lipoparticles, 12 µg/ml; with or without day-7 axotomy; reelin on day 12; surface-biotinylation LRP5 immunoblot.

proposed.why: Isoform varied, readout is surface level of a receptor not shown to bind apoE, a surrogate one step further from B, so class 3, strength 3 like the other non-apoE-receptor surface rows. (was 3/2)

row.Finding description: Adding apoE4 caused a small increase in internalized ApoER2 relative to untreated controls in mouse N2a-APPsw cells.
row.Finding quote: We observed small increases of ApoER2 and β-secretase in response to ApoE and ApoE4 ( Fig. 2 c ), whereas the increase of APP was much greater, ∼2.5 and fourfold in response to ApoE and ApoE4, respectively ( Fig. 2 c ).
row.Finding summary: (no added apoE4 -> added apoE4) -> (more internalized ApoER2)
row.Experimental system: Mouse Neuro-2a neuroblastoma cells stably expressing human Swedish-mutant APP, supplied by Dr. Riqiang Yan, transiently transfected with murine ApoER2 and human β-secretase. Surface proteins were pulse-labeled with cleavable sulfo-NHS-SS-biotin at 4°C, then allowed to internalize for 15 min at 37°C in control medium or medium containing 10 μg/ml apoE4. Surface biotin was stripped with glutathione; protected intracellular biotinylated proteins were recovered with NeutrAvidin agarose and analyzed by Western blot. This was not a human brain-cell system.

proposed.why: Comparator is no added apoE, not apoE3, so apoE4 addition is a surrogate A' (any apoE ligand drives receptor internalization, shown in P7) and surface/internalized receptor is a surrogate B': class 4, strength 4. (was 3/4)

row.Finding description: In normal human fibroblasts, DMPC-apoE4 produced 50% inhibition of LDL binding at 0.036 μg/ml versus 0.039 μg/ml for DMPC-apoE3, indicating slightly stronger competition without a reported significance test.
row.Finding quote: Competition curves comparing LDLR binding by LDL ( Figure 7A ) and dimyristoyl phosphatidylcholine (DMPC) vesicles ( Figure 7B ) indicate that both LDL and DMPC vesicles exhibit a clear dose response, with 50% binding inhibition at 3.44 μg/ml for LDL, and 0.039 and 0.036 μg/ml for E3-DMPC and E4-DMPC, respectively.
row.Finding summary: (DMPC-apoE3 -> DMPC-apoE4) -> (lower concentration required for 50% inhibition of LDLR binding)
row.Experimental system: Normal human fibroblasts cultured for one week before binding assays; donor age and tissue source unspecified. Recombinant human apoE3 or apoE4 was mixed with DMPC at 1:3.75 protein:lipid by weight. Cells were incubated for 2 hours at 4°C with 2 μg/ml radiolabeled human LDL and varying competitor concentrations. LDL binding was measured in triplicate.

proposed.why: Isoform varied and apoE binding to the receptor measured directly (B itself), so class 1, strength 1, same as every other direct binding/affinity/competition row with a defined apoE ligand. (was 1/2)

row.Finding description: With DMPC, Table 4 reports interpolated ³H-LDL binding reductions of 59% for full-length apoE3 and 58% for apoE4. ApoE4 had 99% of apoE3’s normalized LDLR binding ability. The authors described no isoform specificity and supplied no between-isoform significance test.
row.Finding quote: The LDL-R binding ability of apoE- DMPC was higher than that of LDL at the same dose (20-fold), although apoE with or without DMPC did not show isoform specificity.
row.Finding summary: Full-length apoE4 retained 99% of apoE3’s reported LDLR binding ability with DMPC.
row.Experimental system: Human HepG2 hepatoblastoma cells; E. coli-expressed, C-terminally His-tagged human full-length apoE; Table 4 reports 0.5 mg protein with 0.5 mg DMPC. Full-length 0.5 mg responses were interpolated from 0.125 and 1 mg measurements; 3H-LDL competition at 4 °C for 2 h. No receptor-recycling assay.
row.Data location: Table 4, ApoE3 and ApoE4 rows, With DMPC columns

proposed.why: Isoform varied and apoE binding to the receptor measured directly (B itself), so class 1, strength 1, same as every other direct binding/affinity/competition row with a defined apoE ligand. (was 1/2)

row.Finding description: At one apoE molecule per particle, human E4/E4 LpB:E had a lower apparent LDLR dissociation constant than E3/E3 LpB:E, 9.1 versus 16.38±6 nM, indicating stronger binding; the E3/E3 value represented three preparations, whereas the E4/E4 preparation count was unstated.
row.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4, one apoE per LpB:E particle) -> (lower apparent LDLR dissociation constant)
row.Experimental system: Human HeLa cells, a non-brain carcinoma cell line of unspecified source, were preincubated for 48 hours with 10% lipoprotein-deficient serum. Human plasma LpB:E particles were isolated by sequential immunoaffinity chromatography from donors phenotyped E3/E3 or E4/E4; both preparations contained one apoB and one apoE per particle, without apoC-III. Direct iodine-125-labeled lipoprotein binding was measured at 4°C to avoid endocytosis, with a 20-fold excess of unlabeled LDL defining nonspecific binding. Apparent dissociation constants were calculated by Scatchard analysis. Receptor recycling was not measured.
row.Data location: Table 2, LpB:E (n=3; apoE/apoB=1) and LpB E4/E4 rows

proposed.why: Isoform varied and apoE binding to the receptor measured directly (B itself), so class 1, strength 1, same as every other direct binding/affinity/competition row with a defined apoE ligand. (was 1/2)

row.Finding description: The modeled stable LDLR complex dissociated more slowly for fasting APOE3/E4 VLDL1-rich particles than APOE3/E3 particles, with kd2 values of 9.7 versus 11.2 × 10−4 s−1.
row.Finding quote: Relative to the APOE3/E3 group, the dissociation rate constant (kd2) was lower (P = 0.013) and overall K2 was higher (P = 0.032) for the second step of the binding of fasting APOE3/E4 VLDL1-rich particles to the LDLR.
row.Finding summary: (APOE3/E3 -> APOE3/E4) -> (slower stable VLDL1-LDLR complex dissociation)
row.Experimental system: Fasting human male plasma VLDL1-rich TRL, Sf 60–400, pooled from two subjects per sample; trial mean age 48 ± 16 years. LDLR ectodomain SPR, 5 nM apoB, 25 °C, two-state fit; no endosomal pH or recycling assay.

proposed.why: Binding of whole native lipoproteins from genotype-differing donors is a surrogate B' for apoE-receptor adhesion (apoB and particle composition also change), so class 3, strength 3 for all native-particle rows. (was 1/2)

row.Finding description: Postprandial VLDL1-rich particles from APOE3/E4 and APOE3/E3 men showed no significant genotype effect or meal-by-genotype interaction on LDLR binding; genotype-specific values were not presented.
row.Finding quote: There were no significant genotype or meal*genotype interactions observed for the binding of postprandial TRL fractions to the LDLR.
row.Finding summary: (APOE3/E3 -> APOE3/E4) -> (no change in postprandial VLDL1-LDLR binding)
row.Experimental system: Human male crossover trial; VLDL1-rich TRL sampled at individual apoB/apoE peaks, usually 240–360 minutes after SFA, SFA-FO or UNSAT meals; two-subject pools. LDLR ectodomain SPR, 5 nM apoB, 25 °C; no recycling assay.
row.Data location: Results, 'APOE genotype and the binding of postprandial TRL fractions to the LDLR', first sentence; Table 2 presents genotype-combined meal effects

proposed.why: Binding of whole native lipoproteins from genotype-differing donors is a surrogate B' for apoE-receptor adhesion (apoB and particle composition also change), so class 3, strength 3 for all native-particle rows. (was 3/2)

row.Finding description: Fasting VLDL1-rich particles from APOE3/E4 and APOE3/E3 men showed no significant difference in the initial LDLR equilibrium binding constant.
row.Finding summary: (APOE3/E3 -> APOE3/E4) -> (no change in initial VLDL1-LDLR equilibrium binding constant)
row.Experimental system: Fasting human male plasma VLDL1-rich TRL, Sf 60–400, pooled from two subjects per sample; LDLR ectodomain SPR, 5 nM apoB, 25 °C, two-state fit. No receptor recycling measured.

proposed.why: Binding of whole native lipoproteins from genotype-differing donors is a surrogate B' for apoE-receptor adhesion (apoB and particle composition also change), so class 3, strength 3 for all native-particle rows. (was 1/2)

row.Finding description: Fasting VLDL1-rich particles from APOE3/E4 men initially associated with LDLR more slowly than APOE3/E3 particles, with ka1 values of 9.3 versus 11.3 × 10^5 M−1s−1.
row.Finding quote: A slower association rate was also observed with the fasting VLDL1-rich particles from the APOE3/E4 group, but once the VLDL1-LDLR complex was formed, it was found to be more stable and dissociated at a slower rate than the APOE3/E3 VLDL-1 rich fraction.
row.Finding summary: (APOE3/E3 -> APOE3/E4) -> (slower initial VLDL1-LDLR association)
row.Experimental system: Fasting human male plasma VLDL1-rich TRL, Sf 60–400, pooled from two subjects per sample; trial mean age 48 ± 16 years. LDLR ectodomain SPR, 5 nM apoB, 25 °C, two-state fit; no brain cells or recycling assay.

proposed.why: Binding of whole native lipoproteins from genotype-differing donors is a surrogate B' for apoE-receptor adhesion (apoB and particle composition also change), so class 3, strength 3 for all native-particle rows. (was 1/2)

row.Finding description: Fluorescence microscopy of the same binding assay reproduced the isoform pattern, with relative fluorescence printed under the panels as 15.094 ± 1.787 for apoE3 versus 9.880 ± 1.090 for apoE4 (0.65x with apoE4, from 30 cells by ImageJ); the asterisks in the panel mark each apoE condition against control cells, and no apoE4-versus-apoE3 significance is given.
row.Finding quote: These differences among apoE isoforms were also observed under a ﬂuorescence microscope (Fig. 3B).
row.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (qualitatively lower cell-associated particle fluorescence)
row.Experimental system: Human Coriell GM00701 fibroblasts incubated with recombinant human apoE-containing synthetic fluorescent emulsion particles at 2.0 mg/dL apoE for 3 h at 4 °C; fluorescence microscopy at 100× magnification and ImageJ quantification. The legend describes representative images from three independent experiments and relative fluorescence calculated from 30 cells; receptor recycling was not measured.

proposed.why: Isoform varied and apoE binding to the receptor measured directly (B itself), so class 1, strength 1, same as every other direct binding/affinity/competition row with a defined apoE ligand. (was 1/2)
